name: gizza-ai/csv-column-split
summary: Split a CSV column into several columns, or concatenate columns into one.

tool.description: Transform CSV columns in either direction: split one source column into several generated columns by a literal separator (like Text to Columns), or concatenate multiple source columns into one with a chosen separator. Select columns by header name or 1-based index, optionally keep the source columns, trim split values, control maximum split columns, and choose comma/tab/semicolon/pipe CSV delimiters. Returns transformed CSV text.

columns.description: Column or columns to use. In split mode, provide one header name or 1-based index. In concat mode, provide a comma-separated list of header names or 1-based indices in join order.

delimiter.description: CSV field delimiter for both input and output: comma (default), tab, semicolon, or pipe.

has_header.description: Treat the first CSV row as a header row so columns can be selected by name. Default true.

keep_source.description: Keep the original source column(s) as well as the new column(s). Default false replaces the source column(s).

max_columns.description: Split mode only: maximum number of output columns. 0 means split every occurrence; 2 means split on the first occurrence only. Default 0.

mode.description: Operation to perform: split one source column into multiple columns (default), or concat multiple source columns into one.

names.description: Output column names. Split mode: comma-separated names for the generated columns (missing names auto-fill as <source>_1, <source>_2). Concat mode: the combined column name.

separator.description: Literal separator string. Split mode splits cell values on this string; concat mode joins source values with it. Default comma.

trim.description: Split mode only: trim whitespace around each split value. Default true.
